articles.title: Russia’s parliament passes crypto market law with $3,800 annual cap for retail investors
articles.snippet: While citizens still cannot use Bitcoin to buy groceries, the Kremlin is officially letting companies use digital tokens to bypass sanctions and other global trade hurdles.

articles.title: MEXC adds Bittensor TAO staking for its global user base
articles.snippet: The integration with validator Yuma gives millions of MEXC users access to Bittensor, an AI-focused blockchain whose ecosystem now spans 128 specialized subnets.

articles.title: More MiCA-licensed crypto firms may exit EU market: Gate Europe CEO
articles.snippet: Gate Europe’s Giovanni Cunti says some MiCA-licensed crypto firms may struggle to sustain compliance costs as Europe enters its new regulatory era.

articles.title: Pakistan Launches Crypto Investigation Unit to Fight Money Laundering
articles.snippet: Islamabad is building the enforcement side of its crypto push, standing up a unit to police money laundering even as it licenses exchanges.

articles.title: Russia's First Comprehensive Crypto Law Is Two Votes Away From Passing
articles.snippet: The bill licenses exchanges, caps retail investors at about $3,800 a year, and creates a legal pathway for Russian companies to pay foreign partners in crypto—bypassing Western sanctions.
